@frenck thanks and need support as I am not a seasoned developer.
The check black/flake seems to be a layout thing and that is 'easy'
However, the _mapping is not (for me). The way python / sqlalchemy deals with cursors has changed and this is not my piece of cake. The error without _mapping is "tuple indices must be integers or slices, not str" and a aolution would be to change all row[] from strings to integers indicating the column...but this then provides issues in the timetable[]. The _mapping resolves that all and I know no alternative. 
So,
Option 1: someone helps me on this one, and I am happy to learn/test
Option 2: I will abandon the solution/PR as I donot have the time nor the direct interest to learn all of this. IN that case I will keep the solution as a custom_component until someone else has time

EDIT: as _mapping works and I do not understand why this is rejected, this is why I need the support...for me it looks fine and donot see a risk/issue (but then again... I am not (!) a developer)

> The check black/flake seems to be a layout thing and that is 'easy'

Please set up a developing environment, as documented in our developer documentation.
It will help you with those things, and automatically format on commit (alternatively you can run `black` manually.

>  The _mapping resolves that all and I know no alternative.

The `_` underscore indicates it is protected and should, therefore, not be used.

I think the issues you are running into, is that `execute()` now returns a `CursorResult`, which seems to have `all()` available, which you can use instead of `_mapping`.

The juggling with column names could probably be improved by using the `columns()` method on the result: <https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/connections.html#sqlalchemy.engine.Result.columns>

Flippin' nightmare with a slow windows latop but ... well... got it working in 1 hour.

I hope it is fine now as not at all looking forward to fix more than this...spent already way too much time struggling as a non-dev :)

issue_context.title: GTFS AttributeError: 'Engine' object has no attribute 'execute'
issue_context.body:
### The problem

GTFS sensor fails to initialize after creating the SQLite database. 

This data was used: [lr.zip](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/10870810/lr.zip)

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

Home Assistant 2023.3.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

GTFS

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/gtfs/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
- platform: gtfs
    origin: NLR
    destination: ALG
    data: lr.zip
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 293, in _async_setup_platform
    await asyncio.shield(task)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 58, in run
    result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/gtfs/sensor.py", line 510, in setup_platform
    [GTFSDepartureSensor(gtfs, name, origin, destination, offset, include_tomorrow)]

    self._departure = get_next_departure(
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/gtfs/sensor.py", line 345, in get_next_departure
    result = schedule.engine.execute(
AttributeError: 'Engine' object has no attribute 'execute'
```


### Additional information

_No response_

Same issue, different data set
Edit: started with 2023.3, before OK on 2023.2.3

review_comments: This is still accessing a protected method, which should not be used.
as per my comment, with me pylint accepted it where it did not the previous one…and I have reached my limits on understanding how to alternatively do this

This was a **strange** design choice on sqlalchemy's part.  They did this to mirror `namedtuple`

https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.html#collections.somenamedtuple._asdict

It is a documented method though.

https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/connections.html#sqlalchemy.engine.Row._asdict
https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/connections.html#sqlalchemy.engine.Row._mapping
But this code doesn't need to do that. It can just as easily leave `row` as is and change all the `row["yesterday"]` to `row.yesterday` ...etc... instead
But I guess that won't work for https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/89175/files#diff-e1c37923d5176b56acc08bb3063778076c94c5e02ec4c69d92ecf28c1590589eR383
So I think you are stuck with `_asdict()`

Or rewrite the lot ... which very honestly I am not interested in. I'd rather fix the other issues as datetime or even add some things that the SQL is not covering than going into (for me, sorry) nitty-gritty python stuff....I know I know, your comments have a reason too :)
